trigger: Child scores below mastery threshold on sound identification.
strategy: Replay with only two choices, use familiar sounds, and remove visual distractors. Then try 3 new items.
Start with identical sounds versus very different sounds, then increase similarity.
Use clearly contrasted recordings and a simple loud/soft visual scale, keeping volume safe.
Use exaggerated fast/slow patterns with an equal number of sounds.
Return to 2-sound sequences, then increase to 3 only after success.

trigger: Child does not attend to the ending sound when comparing words.
strategy: Use picture pairs with very obvious rhymes.

trigger: Child does not attend to the first sound when comparing words.
strategy: Isolate and exaggerate the first sound before the whole word, use just two very different starting sounds, then reintroduce a wider set.

trigger: Child does not attend to the last sound when comparing words.
strategy: Isolate and exaggerate the final sound after the whole word, use just two very different ending sounds, then reintroduce a wider set.
Compare just two clearly different vowels at a time (e.g. short A vs short U) before mixing in more similar-sounding pairs (short E vs short I).

trigger: Child cannot blend a slowly-spoken word into the whole word.
strategy: Slow the word down further and shorten the gap between sounds, then gradually speed toward normal speech.

trigger: Child cannot count the individual sounds in a word.
strategy: Model tapping one beat per sound while saying the word slowly, then have the child tap along before answering.

trigger: Child cannot connect a letter to its sound, in either direction.
strategy: Drop to just two very different letters (e.g. b and l), practice sound-to-letter only until solid, then reintroduce letter-to-sound.

trigger: Child cannot assemble a word's letters in the correct order.
strategy: Segment the word into its sounds first (return to Module 7's skill), placing one tile immediately after each sound is said, before asking for independent building.

trigger: Child cannot read a written word and match it to its picture.
strategy: Say each letter's sound aloud while pointing to it, then blend slowly left to right (return to Module 6's blending skill) before asking for independent reading.

trigger: Child picks a wrong or extra letter when spelling a dictated word.
strategy: Segment the word into its sounds first (return to Module 7's skill), naming each sound and its letter before removing the extra letters from the tray together.

trigger: Child confuses short and long vowel sounds.
strategy: Compare just one minimal pair at a time (e.g. cap vs cake), exaggerating the long vowel saying its own name, before mixing in other vowels.
